How it works

A managed sales program—not a rep dropped into your Slack.

Capital Generations combines discovery, targeting, sales talent, management, client success, data support, execution, and reporting in one operating model.

  • Clear ICP and qualification standards
  • Prepared and managed sales talent
  • Human-led execution
  • Continuous reporting and adjustment

The operating process

Five stages that turn sales capacity into a working program.

Each stage has a practical output, an owner, and a feedback loop.

01
Align

Define the commercial target.

Clarify the product, value proposition, sales motion, ideal customer, target roles, geographies, qualification criteria, meeting expectations, and success measures.

  • ICP and segment definition
  • Buyer-role priorities
  • Quality and handoff standards
02
Build

Create the market, message, and workflow.

Translate the strategy into target accounts, contact coverage, segmentation, outreach messaging, channel use, CRM stages, and reporting requirements.

  • Account and contact research
  • Messaging frameworks
  • Systems and reporting setup
03
Deploy

Prepare the right team for the engagement.

Assign the SDR or AE capacity, sales manager, client-success lead, and data support required for the scope. Train on the offer, buyer, process, objections, and tools.

  • Talent assignment and onboarding
  • Product and market preparation
  • Manager expectations and KPIs
04
Engage

Run the work with human judgment.

Execute phone-led multichannel outreach, qualification, meeting setting, follow-up, discovery, or opportunity work according to the engagement.

  • Account-aware conversations
  • Documented outcomes and context
  • Defined handoffs and next actions
05
Improve

Use the market response to get better.

Review call feedback, contactability, conversion, meeting outcomes, pipeline movement, and client input. Adjust targeting, messaging, workflow, and coaching accordingly.

  • Performance and strategy reviews
  • Target-market refinement
  • Coaching and accountability action

The working cadence

Accountability happens between the strategy calls.

A good managed program is not a monthly report on activity that already happened. Management, coaching, data work, execution, and adjustment occur continuously.

Daily

Execution and management

Outreach, follow-up, CRM updates, activity monitoring, call review, and rep accountability.

Weekly

Performance and alignment

Review market feedback, activity, outcomes, blockers, upcoming priorities, and client actions.

Ongoing

Data and optimization

Refresh target coverage, improve segmentation, adjust messaging, and respond to performance evidence.

Frequently asked

Process questions

The onboarding and operating plan is tailored to the role, market, and client readiness.

How quickly can a program launch?

Launch timing depends on the role, target market, product complexity, data requirements, systems, and readiness of client materials. The onboarding plan is defined after discovery rather than promised as a generic timeline.

What does the client need to provide?

Clients should provide product and market context, current sales materials, target-customer knowledge, approved claims, CRM or workflow access where required, feedback, and clear ownership for meetings and opportunities.

How often do we review performance?

The engagement includes a regular strategy and performance rhythm. The exact cadence is set with the client and supported by the live reporting view.

Can targeting and messaging change after launch?

Yes. Monitoring and adjustment are core parts of the model. The team uses call feedback, contactability, meeting outcomes, conversion, and client input to improve the program.
